A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPL framework and contain readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting reliable comparison. The supplied v2 ends after its references despite mentioning an appendix; v3 includes Appendices A-D. All supplied material was inspected.

before.justification: V2 reports original PPL results on GenImage, DRCT and Chameleon, together with component ablations, corruption tests and patch-occlusion analyses. These qualify independently of the cited baseline results.

after.justification: V3 retains original PPL experiments and adds benchmark results, extensive ablations, patch-effect distributions and Grad-CAM analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Random Patch Replacement becomes Randomized Patch Reconstruction, but both mix aligned real and diffusion-reconstructed patches; v3 Appendix A confirms the equivalent construction. The margin-based patch loss, combined classification objective and LoRA-tuned CLIP/DINOv2 backbones remain. Algorithm 1 and reconstruction parameters elaborate the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds evaluations on AIGCDetectionBenchmark and UniversalFakeDetect, substantially expanding generator coverage to ProGAN, StyleGAN, CycleGAN and other outputs beyond the earlier benchmarks. GenImage, Chameleon and DRCT remain; renaming DRCT to DRCT-2M does not itself change coverage.

E2.justification: The corruption comparison in Figure 6 expands from UnivFD and DRCT to also include NPR, FatFormer, SAFE, C2P-CLIP and AIDE. New benchmark tables evaluate additional comparators such as LGrad and LNP. Comparator membership in the retained GenImage, DRCT and Chameleon tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 6 changes the reported corruption metric from Accuracy to Balanced Acc and revises blur values from 0.5-2.5 to 0-3 and resizing factors from 0.6-1.4 to 0.5-1.5. New Tables 3-4 compare SDv1.4-trained PPL with GAN-trained baselines, and new ablations introduce additional experimental controls. Newly disclosed default training parameters alone do not establish changed experiments.

E4.justification: V3 adds reconstruction-versus-direct-replacement controls, four hyperparameter sweeps, alternative contrastive losses, fixed-versus-random positions, patch sizes and dropout comparisons. Appendix C adds patch-effect distributions and broader CDE/Grad-CAM analyses, including ConvNeXt. V2's multi-detector masking-recall experiment in Figure 6(b) disappears; the retained single-patch occlusion analysis in Figure 3 is distinct.

E5.justification: Appendix C and Figure 10 add descriptive statistical reporting through violin distributions of normalized patch effects. This does not establish repeated-run uncertainty. No seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are newly supplied; existing across-generator standard deviations are merely reformatted as mean plus/minus standard deviation.

E6.justification: The GenImage, DRCT and Chameleon table scores remain unchanged. V3 adds AIGCDetectionBenchmark mAcc values of 94.41/93.36 and UniversalFakeDetect values of 96.05/93.85 for DINOv2/CLIP, plus numerous analysis results. Module-ablation entries change: LoRA+RPR is 92.6 in v2 Table 4 versus 92.1 in v3 Figure 8's reconstruction series. Revised corruption curves use changed settings and cannot establish same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C introduces exponential normalization of patch effects, exp(TDE(i,j)-TDE_max), and Appendix B adds a computational-cost argument comparing contrastive losses. The core patch-intervention and PCL equations remain equivalent; renaming TDE to CDE does not itself introduce a theoretical result. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same principal contributions: distributed patch artifacts motivate 'All Patches Matter, More Patches Better'; detectors exhibit Few-Patch Bias associated with lazy learning; and PPL improves generalization and robustness. Broader experiments and revised component names support or rephrase these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations connecting matched reconstruction to preserved semantics, interpreting dropout as a weaker remedy for patch reliance, and locating similar bias in CNN decision layers. It removes v2 Section 6's substantive qualification that contemporary generators can exceed academic benchmark quality. The restriction to fully generated images remains.

D1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A newly specify reconstruction strength, denoising steps, guidance, patch size, replacement probabilities, loss parameters, prompt/mask inputs and training pseudocode. Appendix A reports V100 epoch times and 16/19 GB memory without/with PCL, replacing v2's broad 30 GB statement. Unspecified matching conditions prevent interpreting this as a demonstrated efficiency gain.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations including Dual Data Alignment, Seeing Before Reasoning, MSCOCO, Zeiler and Fergus, and several generative-model works. It removes ZED's standalone related-work description while retaining its citation elsewhere. The local-versus-global organization and central positioning against selective patch reliance remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, motivation and methodology undergo extensive rewriting and terminology changes. The experimental narrative shifts from two explicitly named settings to dataset-based comparisons, the standalone limitations section disappears, and structured appendices are added. Author information and conference headers also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces its comparison bars with a radial display and new attention examples; Figure 2 is redesigned. Figure 6 is rebuilt, and the component-ablation table becomes an expanded grouped-bar chart. V3 adds benchmark tables, an algorithm box and numerous appendix displays, while relocating Chameleon results and combining mean/std columns.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially reduces v2's training under-specification and strengthens evidence for the central mechanism through reconstruction, randomization, loss and dropout controls, plus broader patch-utilization analyses. Added benchmarks meaningfully extend transfer evaluation. Removing the limitations discussion and masking comparison weakens balance, and unequal training data limit new baseline comparisons, but the gains in reproducibility and targeted validation provide a substantial net improvement.
